records.body:
=== For Sale: Sealed Bids ===

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The cheque deck holds the values 0 and 2 to 15, 2 of each, for 30 cheques. Each player has a private cheque total starting at 0 and a property hand starting empty. Hands are public.

The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. Played properties are discarded from hands. It is announced publicly who played which property and who took which cheque; running cheque totals stay private.

END: After round 16, each player's final money is their cheque total plus their remaining coins, and these are revealed. The player with the most final money wins. If two or more tie for most, the tied player with more remaining coins wins. If they are still tied, the game is a draw among them and they share the win.

The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. === For Sale: Sealed Bids ===

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The cheque deck holds the values 0 and 2 to 15, 2 of each, for 30 cheques. Each player has a private cheque total starting at 0 and a property hand starting empty. Hands are public.

The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. 3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. records.prompt:
[user]
=== For Sale: Sealed Bids ===

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The cheque deck holds the values 0 and 2 to 15, 2 of each, for 30 cheques. Each player has a private cheque total starting at 0 and a property hand starting empty. Hands are public.

The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. Played properties are discarded from hands. It is announced publicly who played which property and who took which cheque; running cheque totals stay private.

END: After round 16, each player's final money is their cheque total plus their remaining coins, and these are revealed. The player with the most final money wins. If two or more tie for most, the tied player with more remaining coins wins. If they are still tied, the game is a draw among them and they share the win.

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. === For Sale: Sealed Bids ===

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The cheque deck holds the values 0 and 2 to 15, 2 of each, for 30 cheques. Each player has a private cheque total starting at 0 and a property hand starting empty. Hands are public.

The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. Played properties are discarded from hands. It is announced publicly who played which property and who took which cheque; running cheque totals stay private.

END: After round 16, each player's final money is their cheque total plus their remaining coins, and these are revealed. The player with the most final money wins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. === For Sale: Sealed Bids ===

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The cheque deck holds the values 0 and 2 to 15, 2 of each, for 30 cheques. Each player has a private cheque total starting at 0 and a property hand starting empty. Hands are public.

The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. Played properties are discarded from hands. It is announced publicly who played which property and who took which cheque; running cheque totals stay private.

END: After round 16, each player's final money is their cheque total plus their remaining coins, and these are revealed. The player with the most final money wins. === For Sale: Sealed Bids ===

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The cheque deck holds the values 0 and 2 to 15, 2 of each, for 30 cheques. Each player has a private cheque total starting at 0 and a property hand starting empty. Hands are public.

The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. Played properties are discarded from hands. It is announced publicly who played which property and who took which cheque; running cheque totals stay private.

END: After round 16, each player's final money is their cheque total plus their remaining coins, and these are revealed. The player with the most final money wins. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. Played properties are discarded from hands. It is announced publicly who played which property and who took which cheque; running cheque totals stay private.

END: After round 16, each player's final money is their cheque total plus their remaining coins, and these are revealed. The player with the most final money wins. If two or more tie for most, the tied player with more remaining coins wins. If they are still tied, the game is a draw among them and they share the win.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.
records.prompt:
[user]
=== For Sale: Sealed Bids ===

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The cheque deck holds the values 0 and 2 to 15, 2 of each, for 30 cheques. Each player has a private cheque total starting at 0 and a property hand starting empty. Hands are public.

The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. It is announced publicly which player took LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH; bid amounts and coin totals are NOT announced. After round 8 each player holds exactly 8 properties.

SELLING ROUND: In round 9 only, the cheque deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cheques will ever be used. The next 3 cheques from the top are revealed. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. Played properties are discarded from hands. It is announced publicly who played which property and who took which cheque; running cheque totals stay private.

END: After round 16, each player's final money is their cheque total plus their remaining coins, and these are revealed. The player with the most final money wins. If two or more tie for most, the tied player with more remaining coins wins. If they are still tied, the game is a draw among them and they share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Each round runs in this order: reveal properties → buying view → sealed bid → rank the bids → take the properties → reveal cheques → selling view → choose a property → sell the properties → advance the round → final money → after round 16.

Actions you may be asked for:
  sealed_bid   answer with a whole number, in the range you are given
  choose_a_property answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. 3 players. Each starts with 18 coins; your coin total is private, only you see it. The property deck holds the cards 1 to 30, one of each (30 cards). The game lasts 16 rounds. Rounds 1-8 are BUYING rounds and rounds 9-16 are SELLING rounds.

BUYING ROUND: In round 1 only, the property deck is shuffled; only the top 24 cards will ever be used and the bottom 6 stay unseen. The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1). The first-ranked player takes HIGH and pays their full bid (a bid of 7 costs 7). The second-ranked player takes MIDDLE and pays half their bid, rounded down. The third-ranked player takes LOW and pays half their bid, rounded down (a bid of 5 costs 2). Payments go to the bank and come out of each player's private coins. All players at the same moment secretly choose one property from their own hand. The chosen properties are revealed; properties are all different, so there are no ties. The player who played the highest property adds the highest cheque to their cheque total. The middle property gets the middle cheque, and the lowest property gets the lowest cheque. Played properties are discarded from hands. It is announced publicly who played which property and who took which cheque; running cheque totals stay private.

The next 3 cards from the top are revealed, called LOW, MIDDLE and HIGH by value. All players at the same moment secretly submit a bid: a whole number from 0 up to their current coins. Bids are ranked from highest to lowest. Ties are broken by this round's priority order: in round r, priority goes first to player ((r-1) mod 3)+1, then to the next player number, wrapping 3 to 1 (in round 2 the order is 2, 3, 1).
